title: Export data as a CSV download
when: The user wants a button that downloads table or list data as a CSV file that opens correctly in spreadsheet programs.
prompt:
Goal: A correct, safe CSV built in the browser and downloaded with a clear name, keeping accents intact.
Steps:
1. Define columns explicitly as { label, get: (row) => value } so order and headers are fixed.
2. Escape each field: to string; if it contains a comma, quote, \r or \n, wrap in quotes and double inner quotes.
3. Guard formula injection: prefix a single quote to user values starting with =, +, - or @.
4. Join fields with commas and rows with \r\n; prepend \uFEFF so spreadsheets read UTF-8 accents.
5. Download via new Blob([text], { type: "text/csv;charset=utf-8" }), URL.createObjectURL, a temporary <a download="orders-2026-10-17.csv">, click, then revoke the URL a moment later.
6. Export what the user sees (filters and sort applied) and say it on the button (Export 42 rows).
Quality bar:
- Dates ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) and dot decimals unless local formats were asked.
- File name has subject and date.
- 100 thousand rows build without freezing.
Pitfalls:
- Joining values with commas and no quoting.
- Leaking hidden or private columns.
- Revoking the object URL before the download starts.
Verify:
- [ ] Escaping handles quotes, commas and line breaks.
- [ ] BOM present.
- [ ] Name ends in .csv with a date.
- [ ] Button has a label and type="button".
Output: js/export-csv.js exporting toCSV(rows, columns) and downloadCSV(name, text), wired to a button.

examples.input: botão para baixar a lista de vendas em csv
examples.output: Export 120 rows button building vendas-2026-10-17.csv with quoted fields and a BOM
